title: Register a vehicle for local personal property tax
question: I moved to Charlottesville or bought a car. Do I have to tell the Commissioner of the Revenue?
office: Commissioner of the Revenue, City of Charlottesville (elected constitutional officer); billing and collection by the City Treasurer
summary: Yes. Charlottesville taxes vehicles normally garaged in the city, and the Commissioner of the Revenue assesses them. The city says to register with the Commissioner's Office within 30 days of moving here or of buying a vehicle. If your DMV record shows Charlottesville as the garage jurisdiction, DMV should pass it on; if not, contact the office by phone, email or in person. There is no decal. The tax is prorated by month, reduced by state car tax relief on qualifying personal vehicles, and billed by the City Treasurer in two halves due June 5 and December 5. Students taxed at home and service members here on orders are not taxed here.

steps.step: Title and register the vehicle in Virginia with its Charlottesville address
steps.who: Vehicle owner; Virginia DMV, or the City's DMV Select office in the Treasurer's Office at City Hall
steps.how: If you bought the vehicle, apply to DMV for a Virginia title within 30 days of the purchase. If you moved to Virginia from another state, you may drive a passenger car, pickup or panel truck, moped, autocycle or motorcycle that is registered for the current year in that state, with its plates, for your first 30 days of residency; then register it in Virginia. If you moved, tell DMV your new address within 30 days. The City's DMV Select office in the first-floor lobby of City Hall (605 East Main Street) handles original titles and registrations, 8:30 am to 4:15 pm, Monday to Friday except holidays. A non-resident active-duty service member (or activated or mobilized reserve or National Guard member) living here need not title or register in Virginia a vehicle registered and titled in another state (Va. Code § 46.2-600). If your DMV record shows Charlottesville as the garage jurisdiction, the city says DMV should forward it to the Commissioner (step s2).
steps.deadline: within 30 days of the purchase or transfer (title); the first 30 days of residency (driving on out-of-state plates); within 30 days of a move (address change)
steps.fee: DMV title and registration fees, set by the state (not covered here)
steps.quote: shall, within 30 days of the purchase or transfer, apply to the Department for a certificate of ownership.

steps.step: New resident: register with the Commissioner of the Revenue within 30 days of moving here
steps.who: Vehicle owner (new resident), to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: If you changed your vehicle record at DMV to show Charlottesville as the garage jurisdiction, the city says DMV should forward it to the Commissioner. If you have not, the city says to contact the Commissioner's Office immediately: call 434-970-3160, email citycor@charlottesville.gov, or go to the Customer Service window in City Hall (605 E Main Street, Room A-130, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday). The city publishes no separate form for this. In either case, the city says you should also register with the office within 30 days of moving here.
steps.quote: You should also register with the Commissioner’s Office for personal property tax within 30 days of moving here.

steps.step: Bought a vehicle: register it with the Commissioner of the Revenue within 30 days of becoming the owner
steps.who: Vehicle owner (buyer), to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Tell the Commissioner's Office about the vehicle by phone, email or in person, as in step s2. If it replaces a vehicle you sold, traded or junked, also report the old one with the city's Disposed Personal Property online form (f4); the paper Request for Refund or Prorated Assessment form (f5) covers the same notice. The city says DMV and the Commissioner must be told of a sale within 30 days, and that this is the owner's own duty, not the dealer's or the new owner's (FAQ QID=489). If the disposal is reported to DMV more than 30 days after it happened, the city uses the reporting date as the disposal date for tax purposes unless you provide proper documentation, such as a bill of sale (Report page).
steps.deadline: within 30 days of purchasing (or otherwise becoming the owner) of a vehicle
steps.quote: Virginia law requires you to register with the locality of your jurisdiction within 30 days of purchasing (or otherwise becoming the owner) of a vehicle.

steps.step: Check whether you are taxed elsewhere or exempt (students, military, disabled veterans)
steps.who: Vehicle owner; the Commissioner of the Revenue decides
steps.how: A full-time student at a college or university in Charlottesville is not taxed here if the vehicle is taxed in the student's domicile; state law lets the city ask for evidence of that tax. A Charlottesville resident attending college elsewhere is taxed here. Active-duty service members who, with their spouses, are in Charlottesville by virtue of military orders are not liable here; send a copy of your most recent Leave and Earnings Statement to claim this. A service member who keeps Charlottesville as legal residence, with the vehicle registered in Virginia, is liable here wherever stationed. A veteran rated 100% service-connected, permanently and totally disabled can exempt one passenger car, pickup or panel truck registered for personal use: owned by the veteran, jointly with the spouse, or by the spouse and used primarily by or for the veteran. Apply on the city's form with the VA certification; the form says you must reapply if you change vehicles. The exemption runs from the date the vehicle is acquired (never before January 1, 2021) and ends at the veteran's death; it does not pass to a surviving spouse. Leased vehicles, business-owned vehicles and vehicles held in a trust do not qualify for the veteran exemption.
steps.quote: If you are a full-time student attending an institution of higher learning in Charlottesville, you would not be liable here if you are paying a personal property tax on the vehicle in your domicile.

steps.step: The Commissioner assesses the vehicle and prorates the tax by month
steps.how: The Commissioner values cars and trucks at the NADA clean trade-in value. Motorcycles are valued from the NADA motorcycle guide, and trailers at a percentage of original cost. A vehicle that arrives in the city, or is bought, after January 1 is taxed by the month, for the months it is garaged in the city and owned by you. More than half a month counts as a full month. If you do not file a required return, state law says the Commissioner shall still assess the vehicle at fair market value from the best information he can obtain. To ask for a lower value for high mileage, a branded title, or a DMV salvage or non-repairable certificate, see step s8.
steps.deadline: ownership and value are fixed as of January 1 (the tax day), or as of the day the vehicle acquires a situs in the city
steps.quote: In general terms, a vehicle’s tax will be prorated on a monthly basis based on the number of months it has a situs in the City of Charlottesville or is owned by the taxpayer.

steps.step: Check that the bill gives the vehicle car tax relief (PPTR)
steps.who: Vehicle owner; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Car tax relief applies to the first $20,000 of value of a passenger car, pickup or panel truck, or motorcycle. The city says the vehicle must be owned by a natural person, or leased by a natural person under a contract requiring that person to pay the tax, and used for nonbusiness purposes. State law also counts an autocycle, and a vehicle held in a private trust for nonbusiness purposes (Va. Code § 58.1-3523); the city FAQ does not mention these. City Council sets the relief percentage each year (31% for 2025). If the vehicle is worth $1,500 or less, the tax is eliminated. A vehicle counts as used for business, and does not qualify, if more than 50% of its mileage is deducted as a business expense or reimbursed by an employer, more than 50% of its depreciation is deducted, its cost is expensed under Internal Revenue Code § 179, or it is leased and the leasing company pays the tax without reimbursement. Review the bill, and contact the Commissioner if the vehicle is qualified wrongly. The city treats paying the bill as your acknowledgement that the qualification is correct. The city audits income tax schedules; if they show more than 50% business mileage, relief is withdrawn by a supplemental assessment with late payment penalty and interest, for the current and up to three prior tax years.
steps.fee: relief percentage set each year by City Council (2025: 31%, applied to the first $20,000 of value)
steps.quote: Citizens are obligated to thoroughly review information detailed on their tax bills to ensure their vehicles are properly qualified.

steps.step: Pay the City Treasurer's bill in two installments
steps.who: City Treasurer (bills and collects); vehicle owner (pays)
steps.how: The Treasurer mails the bill. The first installment, which includes the city vehicle license fee, is due June 5; the second is due December 5. If a due date falls on a weekend, it moves to the following Monday. The city issues no decal. You can pay: online through the city's payment link; by mail to City of Charlottesville Treasurer's Office, P.O. Box 2854, Charlottesville, VA 22902 (the U.S. Post Office postmark, not a meter stamp, decides timeliness); at the City Hall customer service counter (cash, check, debit card or money order; no credit cards for taxes there); in the City Hall drop boxes (checks and money orders); or by card at 866-660-5185. If you cannot pay in full, call the Treasurer's Office at 434-970-3146 about a payment arrangement. Penalty and interest still apply under an arrangement. Members of the armed services deployed outside the United States get an automatic extension on the tax on a qualifying vehicle, due 90 days after the deployment ends (Va. Code § 58.1-3916). The Treasurer's 2016 Late Payment Penalty Policy says not receiving a bill is no ground for waiving penalty, so contact the office before the due date if no bill arrives. Unpaid taxes can lead to withholding of state income tax refunds or lottery winnings, DMV vehicle registration withholding, and tax liens.
steps.fee: $4.40 per $100 of assessed value, less car tax relief; city vehicle license fee in the first installment (amount not found); 10% late payment penalty and 10% a year interest
steps.quote: Taxes are due on June 5th and December 5th of each year.

steps.step: If the assessment is wrong, apply to the Commissioner of the Revenue for a correction
steps.who: Vehicle owner, to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Send an application for correction, made in good faith, with your name, identification number, account number, address and phone number. Include a copy of the assessment, a written statement of why it is wrong and how you worked that out, the papers you rely on, the relief you want, and the name of a contact person to arrange an inspection of the vehicle if one is needed. Supporting papers can include a branded title, a DMV certificate, or the High Mileage Application (f3; passenger vehicles only), whose supporting document must show the VIN and be dated before January 1. On request, the Commissioner reduces the value for condition: a water-damage title by 20%, a rebuilt or repaired title by 50%, a salvage certificate by 75%, and a non-repairable certificate by 90%; the city's sheet says an additional form may be required and should show the condition before January 1. The Commissioner may ask for more information and may hold an informal conference. The city's sheet says filing does not extend the due date and that penalty and interest may apply, so pay on time (see the escalation rung on collection during an appeal filed within 90 days). You may ask for the decision's facts and law in writing.
steps.deadline: within three years from the last day of the tax year or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later (Va. Code § 58.1-3980(A)); the Commissioner answers in writing within 90 days of a complete application
steps.quote: Within 90 days of receipt of a complete application for correction, the Commissioner of the Revenue will thoroughly review and analyze said application and notify the taxpayer in writing of his determination.

caveats: The 30-day deadlines for registering with the Commissioner come from the city's FAQ answers (Faq.aspx?QID=488 and QID=490). QID=490 says 'Virginia law requires' it. The state sections read set a January 1 tax day and a May 1 return (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3515, 58.1-3518), and let a locality require a new return when a vehicle is acquired or changes situs (Va. Code § 58.1-3518.1(B)), but none of them sets a 30-day deadline for telling the Commissioner. That deadline probably comes from the City Code (Chapter 30, Taxation), which was not read. The 30-day DMV deadlines are state law (Va. Code §§ 46.2-600, 46.2-606, 46.2-662).

Local ordinance not checked. The city links its Code of Ordinances to Municode. Municode's terms of use could not be read (its terms page answered HTTP 520), and its content API refuses unauthenticated requests, so no City Code text is quoted. A search-engine summary of city WebLink records mentioned City Code § 30-31 (recognized pricing guide), Chapter 30, Article II, Division 2 (§ 30-51 et seq., personal property tax relief) and § 15-36 (vehicle licensing). These are unverified hints and have not been checked.

The amount of the city vehicle license fee was not found on any current city page read. The FAQ (QID=487) says only that vehicles with active plates are charged the fee in the first installment. State law caps it at the state registration fee in effect on January 1, 2020 (Va. Code § 46.2-752(A)).

Tax rate and relief year: the FAQ calls $4.40 per $100 the 'current' rate. The Treasurer's Personal Property Taxes page gives $4.40 'For tax year 2024'. The FAQ lists relief rates only through 2025 (31%). A 2026 City Council resolution on the city's WebLink records system could not be opened (WebLink returned an error), so no 2026 rate or relief percentage is recorded. Confirm the current year's rate and relief percentage with the Commissioner.

No form for registering a newly acquired vehicle, or a new resident's vehicle, was found on the Forms Index or the Personal Property Tax page. The FAQ says DMV 'should' forward a Charlottesville garage jurisdiction and otherwise directs people to contact the office. How the office takes the details (phone, email or counter) is not described. The Disposed Personal Property and address-change forms are online Laserfiche forms that render only with JavaScript; their fields were not read.

Proration timing for mid-year arrivals: the city prorates monthly (FAQ QID=484). State law lets a locality bill partial-year taxes on or after December 15 with a due date at least 30 days later (Va. Code § 58.1-3516(B)). Whether Charlottesville bills newly registered vehicles on the June 5 and December 5 cycle or on a separate supplemental bill was not stated on the pages read.

Appeals and penalties: the city's Administrative Appeals sheet says filing does not extend the due date and that penalty and interest may apply. Va. Code § 58.1-3916 says a bill is not delinquent or subject to collection procedures while an appeal filed within 90 days of the assessment is pending, and for 30 days after the decision. Paying by the due date is the safe course.

Va. Code § 58.1-3983.1 gives a Tax Commissioner appeal only for 'local mobile property tax' (airplanes, boats, campers, recreational vehicles and trailers) and business taxes. For an ordinary passenger car, pickup or motorcycle, the route after the Commissioner of the Revenue is the circuit court.

Military: the FAQ (QID=491) bases the service-member rule on the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act. That federal law is not in the 'va' index and is not quoted here. The state deployment extension (Va. Code § 58.1-3916) is quoted. The Treasurer's late-payment penalty policy is the 2016 edition (DOC). It cites Va. Code § 46.2-754, which now concerns Arlington County only; the general DMV registration-withholding authority is Va. Code § 46.2-752(J). The Treasurer's Personal Property Taxes page lists 'DMV vehicle registration withholding' among its collection procedures.

Whether Charlottesville has adopted the optional local penalty of up to $250 for a vehicle not registered in Virginia after a new resident's first 30 days (Va. Code § 46.2-662(B)), or imposes a failure-to-file penalty on late vehicle registration, was not found. Only the state caps are recorded.

The Payment Methods page is internally inconsistent about online fees. It says 'There is no convenience fee for tax payments made online' right after stating a 2.59% credit card fee. The Treasurer's Personal Property Taxes page says there is no fee for ACH or electronic check. The fee entry records the card fees as stated.

Contact notes: the Treasurer's page also shows citytreas@charlottesville.org; the .gov address from its 'Email the City Treasurer' link is recorded. The Request for Refund or Prorated Assessment form (dated 10/14/15) gives an older charlottesville.org mailbox and asks for Social Security numbers; that mailbox is not recorded. Staff names shown on the office pages and forms are not recorded.

Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia renders the section sign as a replacement character, so state-law quotes were chosen or cut to avoid it. DMV's own title and registration fees and documents are not covered here (state agency).

Delinquency costs: the Treasurer's 2016 Late Payment Penalty Policy restates Va. Code § 58.1-3958, under which a locality may add administrative costs of up to $30 (collected 30 or more days after a delinquency notice, before judgment) or $35 (after judgment), plus attorney's or collection agency fees of up to 20%. It also says a fee for removing a DMV registration withholding is added to the tax due. Whether the city currently charges these, and the amount of the withholding fee, were not found on a current page, so they are not listed as fees.

Some step details come from pages other than the step's cited URL: in s3, the sale-notice duty is from FAQ QID=489 and the late-disposal rule from the Report page (/1106/Report); in s4, the military rule is from FAQ QID=491 and the veteran exemption from the Personal Property Tax page (/190) and the veteran form (f1); in s7, the payment methods are from the Payment Methods page (/562) and the no-bill rule from the 2016 Late Payment Penalty Policy.

corrections: s2: the draft told readers to 'register with the office within 30 days' as a flat command. The FAQ (QID=488) says 'should', and that DMV 'should' forward the record. The step now keeps the city's 'should' and attributes both points to the city.

s1: the draft said a DMV record is how the Commissioner 'usually' learns of a vehicle; no source says that. It now says the city expects DMV to forward the record. It adds that § 46.2-662(A) covers only passenger cars, pickup or panel trucks, mopeds, autocycles and motorcycles registered for the current year in the other state, and the § 46.2-600 exception for non-resident active-duty service members with out-of-state title and registration.

s5: the draft said the Commissioner 'can still assess' an unreported vehicle. § 58.1-3519 says the Commissioner 'shall' assess it from the best information he can obtain. The wording now follows the statute.

s6: 'owned by a person' is now 'a natural person', as the FAQ and § 58.1-3523 say. It adds the state-law qualifying categories the FAQ leaves out (autocycles; vehicles held in a private trust for nonbusiness purposes), quoted from § 58.1-3523. It also adds the FAQ's full business-use tests and its audit rule: relief is withdrawn for the current and up to three prior years if income tax schedules show more than 50% business mileage.

s4: added from the FAQ (QID=491, QID=492) that a service member whose legal residence is Charlottesville is liable wherever stationed, and that a city resident at college elsewhere is taxed here. From the veteran form (f1) and § 58.1-3668(B)-(C), it adds spouse ownership, reapplication on a change of vehicle, the start date (never before January 1, 2021) and the end at the veteran's death. Two § 58.1-3668(C) quotes are added to legal_basis.

s7: added the automatic extension that § 58.1-3916 says the locality 'shall allow' for deployed service members (new legal_basis quote); that drop boxes take checks and money orders, and that a postal meter stamp does not count (Payment Methods page); that not receiving a bill is no ground for a waiver (2016 policy); and the Treasurer's collection measures (refund and lottery setoff, DMV registration withholding, liens).

s8: completed the application contents from the Administrative Appeals sheet: identification number, the contact person for an inspection, condition shown as before January 1, and the Commissioner's power to ask for more information and hold an informal conference. It names the High Mileage Application (f3), which is for passenger vehicles only and needs a document showing the VIN dated before January 1. It also points to the § 58.1-3916 collection hold. A § 58.1-3503(B) quote is added: the Commissioner 'shall upon request' take condition into account.

s3: added, from FAQ QID=489 (now in sources), the 30-day sale notice to DMV and the Commissioner. From the Report page it adds that a disposal reported to DMV more than 30 days late is dated by the report unless you document it. The paper refund and proration form (f5) is now linked from a step.

Escalation (Tax Commissioner rung): added airplanes, which are in the § 58.1-3983.1(A) definition of local mobile property tax. It also adds the one-year deadline for the underlying § 58.1-3983.1(B)(1) appeal, which is shorter than the three years of § 58.1-3980(A). The new § 58.1-3983.1(B)(1) quote is in legal_basis and the basis cites (B)(1).
Escalation (§ 58.1-3980(B) rung): the trigger now includes the statute's condition that the taxpayer 'can demonstrate by clear factual evidence' that he was not subject to the tax.

Caveats: the draft recorded a 2026 relief figure (31%) taken from a search-engine summary of a resolution that was never read. That unverified figure is removed. Two caveats are added: one on delinquency costs and DMV withholding fees (2016 policy, § 58.1-3958), and one naming the pages that support details not on a step's cited URL. FAQ QID=489 is added to sources, and §§ 46.2-754 and 58.1-3958 are added to the state-law source list.
open_issues: City Code (Municode) not read. The 30-day registration rule is stated only in the city FAQ ('Virginia law requires', QID=490); no state section read sets it. The steps attribute it to the city, so step correctness is not affected.
The amount of the city vehicle license fee was not found on any current city page (the Treasurer's 'Vehicle License Fees' quick link goes to the Personal Property Tax page, which has no amount).
The current-year (2026) tax rate and relief percentage are not confirmed. The FAQ calls $4.40 'current', and the Treasurer's page dates it to tax year 2024.

Not stated: whether newly registered vehicles get a separate supplemental bill (§ 58.1-3516(B)), whether the city has adopted the § 46.2-662(B) penalty or a failure-to-file penalty, and whether it charges § 58.1-3958 administrative costs.

The Payment Methods page contradicts itself on the online card fee. The city's Administrative Appeals sheet says penalty and interest may apply during an appeal. § 58.1-3916 says a bill is not delinquent while an appeal filed within 90 days is pending, and for 30 days after the decision. Both are noted and the statute is quoted.
The federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act is not in the va index and is not quoted.
